Executive Summary Airport operations are expanding, with growing electrical loads that could exceed local grid capacity limitations. Installing additional capacity to support this load growth can be costly and time-consuming. The Athena project has developed a load forecast model, Aeroportal, to predict the future grid capacity that would be needed for these new loads. These models also reveal the potential for on-site distributed energy resources (DER)—battery energy storage systems (BESS) and photovoltaics (PV)—and flexible load management to mitigate the need for these upgrades. This report outlines the development of multiple smart charge management (SCM) load management solutions—Gold and Platinum with and without DER—that coordinate flexible loads with DER assets to avoid exceeding grid capacity limitations. The Gold control is a purely heuristic-based control, while the Platinum control is a forecast-based optimization that requires detailed information regarding electric vehicle (EV) reservation schedules. Table ES-1 outlines the summary of results from the testing of each control with a few key conclusions: 1. The Platinum-based control consistently outperforms the Gold control by improving delivered state-of-charge (SOC) metrics. 2. Each control performs better when paired with DER, as both offer a significant reduction in capital investments compared to the uncontrolled capacity upgrade. 3. The SCM results in some SOC performance compromise to support capacity limits, with the Platinum DER control nearly matching the uncontrolled scenario but at a lower cost. 4. SOC performance compromises highlight the challenges with short dwell times that eliminate the option for some EVs to complete their charge session under any scenario. Table ES-1. This real-time emulation stress test proves the technology could be easily adapted for field demonstrations with equipment available today. These findings present exciting opportunities for fleets to address peak demand challenges that may be increasing utility bills or delaying expanding operations.
